```{r}
# --- DER FIX: DATENTYPEN KORRIGIEREN ---

# 1. Daten laden
all_data <- readRDS("cleaned_survey_data.rds")

# 2. Vorbereiten & Typen umwandeln (WICHTIG!)
regression_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Wir zwingen R, diese Spalten als Zahlen zu behandeln
    # (as.character stellt sicher, dass Faktoren korrekt umgewandelt werden)
    Numerical_Infl_Exp_YR = as.numeric(as.character(Numerical_Infl_Exp_YR)),
    Categorical_Infl_Exp_YR = as.numeric(as.character(Categorical_Infl_Exp_YR)),
    age = as.numeric(as.character(age)),
    
    time_decimal = year + (quarter - 1) / 4,
    time_factor = factor(time_decimal),
    
    age_group = case_when(
      age < 40 ~ "Young",
      age >= 40 & age <= 60 ~ "Middle",
      age > 60 ~ "Old",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    )
  )

# 3. Aggregieren (Jetzt sollte mean() funktionieren!)
cohort_data <- regression_data %>%
  group_by(time_decimal, time_factor, age_group) %>%
  summarise(
    p_up = mean(Categorical_Infl_Exp_YR %in% c(1, 2), na.rm = TRUE),
    p_down = mean(Categorical_Infl_Exp_YR == 5, na.rm = TRUE),
    pi_measured = mean(Numerical_Infl_Exp_YR, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 4. Training
# Wir filtern NaNs und NAs raus
training_data <- cohort_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(pi_measured)) %>%
  mutate(time_factor = droplevels(time_factor))

# Check: Jetzt sollten hier ca. 300-500 Zeilen stehen
print(paste("Zeilen im Training-Set:", nrow(training_data)))

if(nrow(training_data) > 10) {
  model <- lm(pi_measured ~ p_up + p_down + time_factor, data = training_data)
  
  # 5. Imputation anwenden
  b_up   <- coef(model)["p_up"]
  b_down <- coef(model)["p_down"]
  const  <- coef(model)["(Intercept)"]
  
  cohort_data <- cohort_data %>%
    mutate(imputed_inflation = const + (b_up * p_up) + (b_down * p_down))
  
  print("Die Imputation ist fertig.")
  head(cohort_data)
} else {
  print("Fehler")
}
```

```{r}
library(zoo) # Für den gleitenden Durchschnitt

# 1. Daten glätten (4-Quartals-Durchschnitt wie im Paper)
plot_data_mn <- cohort_data %>%
    filter(age_group != "Unknown") %>%
    arrange(age_group, time_decimal) %>%
    group_by(age_group) %>%
    mutate(
        # Wir berechnen einen gleitenden Durchschnitt über 4 Quartale
        smoothed_inflation = rollmean(imputed_inflation, k = 4, fill = NA, align = "right")
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

# 2. Grafik im M&N Stil
ggplot(plot_data_mn, aes(x = time_decimal, y = smoothed_inflation, color = age_group)) +
    # Die Linien (etwas dicker für den Look)
    geom_line(size = 1.2) +
    # Farbwahl: M&N nutzen oft Schwarz/Grau-Töne oder sehr kontrastreiche Farben
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Young" = "#E41A1C", "Middle" = "#377EB8", "Old" = "#4DAF4A")) +
    # Achsen-Design wie im Wirtschaftsjournal
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1950, 2025, 10), expand = c(0,0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
    labs(
        title = "Figure 1: Mean Inflation Expectations by Age Group",
        subtitle = "4-quarter moving average of imputed expectations",
        x = "Year",
        y = "Expected Inflation",
        color = "Cohort"
    ) +
    # Professionelles "White-Grid" Theme
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        text = element_text(family = "serif"), # Serifenschrift für den Paper-Look
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
    )
```
